solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'E tucked into girl's meat

indicators.note: tucked into means one piece is pushed inside the other, here the dropped-aitch pronoun inside the name

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
'E is he with the aitch dropped, giving just the letter E

explanation.surface: A cockney man tucks into a girl's dinner of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the flesh of a calf eaten as food, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Second prize for pirate

definitions.meaning: the runner-up gets a medal made of the grey precious metal, after gold
Long John ... is the one-legged pirate of Stevenson's Treasure Island

explanation.surface: Coming second in a contest wins a prize meant for a buccaneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympic runners-up take the second-place medal; Stevenson's famous buccaneer is Long John of that surname.

clue.text: Give gear mistakenly, causing distress

indicators.note: doing something mistakenly gets it wrong, so the letters of the two words are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Handing someone the wrong equipment upsets them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' signals an anagram of GIVE GEAR; 'causing' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress someone is to upset or wrong them, which is what the verb means: to cause grievance.

clue.text: High temperature not starting at any time

indicators.note: not starting means the word for a high temperature loses its opening letter

parts.note: a fever is a high body temperature

explanation.surface: A patient whose high temperature never seems to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb used in questions like 'have you been there?' means on any occasion whatsoever.

clue.text: Elves wandering around close to this craft

indicators.note: around means the shuffled elves are placed about the final letter of this
wandering elves stray from their places, so the letters of the word are mixed up
close to means the end, so only the final letter of the word this is taken

explanation.surface: Elves roam about near some boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns ELVES into VESEL, and 'around' puts it about S, the last letter of 'this' ('close to').
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is a boat or ship, and a vessel is a ship or boat too.

clue.text: Furious, means to escape across English border

indicators.note: across means the escape route stretches over the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a vent is an outlet, a way for gas or steam to escape
a hem is the edge or border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone livid and plotting a getaway over the English frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement describes strong, passionate feeling, so an angry, forceful outburst fits it.

clue.text: Annoying very old partner, one no good

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former partner who was useless is very annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating or troublesome, such as a long-running problem, is annoying in just this sense.

clue.text: Gutted, venerable European socialist changed direction

indicators.note: something gutted has its insides removed, so only the outer letters of venerable remain

parts.note: red is the colour associated with socialists, and a common name for one

explanation.surface: A disappointed elderly European left-winger swung the other way politically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like British slang for disappointed, but it empties VENERABLE down to VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to swerve or change course suddenly, so the past tense means turned away.

clue.text: More intelligent installing bar in church? Right!

indicators.note: installing means the church abbreviation takes the bar into its middle

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lever is a rigid bar used to prise or move things

explanation.surface: Fitting a crossbar in a church would be smarter, wouldn't it? Correct!
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of clever means brighter or smarter, having more intellect.

clue.text: Turning back periodically unnerves Swede, perhaps

indicators.note: turning back means the chosen letters are read in the opposite direction
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of unnerves is taken

explanation.surface: A Swede on the way back gets rattled every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the even letters of uNnErVeS, NEVS; 'Turning back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sven is a common Scandinavian man's name, so it is an example of a Swede, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Suddenly turn to render assistance, grabbing wife

indicators.note: grabbing means the helping word clutches the letter for wife within it

parts.note: to serve is to help or give service to someone

explanation.surface: A driver swings the car round to help, catching hold of his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer sharply to one side, as a car does to avoid an obstacle.

clue.text: At unspecified place in meadow, he reverses

indicators.note: in means the letters run inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Somewhere out in a field, a man backs his vehicle up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' tempts a reversal, but the letters read forwards in meadoW HE REVERses.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in or to whatever location, a place left unstated.

clue.text: Worked out only daughter's about five

indicators.note: about means the first pieces wrap round the Roman five

parts.note: sole means only, as in sole survivor
V is the Roman numeral for five
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone calculates that their only daughter is roughly five years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately', but it places SOLE+D around V.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that has been cracked or figured out has been solved.

clue.text: Voter, say, unexpectedly to be a Remainer?

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly is out of the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A voter who surprisingly backs staying in the EU in the Brexit referendum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remainer' suggests Brexit, but it here means one who remains, staying the night as a guest; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend the night at someone's house is to remain there, being one who lingers rather than leaves.

clue.text: US ex-serviceman, seventy-five today? Much less than that

indicators.note: much less than the whole phrase means only a short run of letters inside it is taken

explanation.surface: An American veteran turns seventy-five today — or is he far younger?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in seventy-fiVE Today. The puzzle marked VE (Victory in Europe) Day's 75th anniversary, 8 May 2020; every answer contains VE.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the short form of veteran means someone who formerly served in the armed forces.

clue.text: Struggle to eat what's laid for breakfast? One would if it's bacon

indicators.note: to eat means the word for struggle takes the breakfast item inside it

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
an egg is laid by a hen and eaten for breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to eat their cooked breakfast; anyone would, if bacon is on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: the definition leans on the wordplay, since a vegetarian would struggle to eat breakfast that is bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian refuses meat, so would struggle to eat a breakfast of bacon; the colloquial short form names such a person.

clue.text: Crawl, lazily, at first, beneath small plantation

indicators.note: beneath means, in a down clue, the first letter of lazily sits below the trees

parts.note: a grove is a small wood or orchard of trees

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word lazily is taken

explanation.surface: Something creeps idly along under a small orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: To grovel is to abase oneself, to fawn or creep, which is to crawl in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Prevents vast reforms overwhelming monarch

indicators.note: overwhelming means the reformed letters engulf the royal abbreviation
reforms means the letters of vast are formed again in a new order

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: Sweeping reforms that swamp the sovereign stop something happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' gives AVTS, which 'overwhelming' wraps round the monarch; 'reforms' reads as a noun in the surface but works as the anagram verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to ward it off or stop it occurring.

clue.text: Football or cricket team's prime?

parts.note: a football or cricket side has this many players, and the number is also a prime

explanation.surface: Asking which players are a sports team's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime' suggests the team's best players, but it means a prime number.
explanation.definitionFit: Both football and cricket field sides of that many players, and the number divides only by itself and one.

clue.text: 14 having zero power to stop

parts.note: 14 points to the answer to 14-across, a US ex-serviceman
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A cross-reference giving the power to halt something.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the right to block or reject a decision, a power of refusal.

clue.text: Better than average sort of pea — bravo!

indicators.note: sort here works as a verb, to sort or arrange the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper cheering a kind of pea.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a score over the standard is worse, so the idiom for being better than the norm means superior.

clue.text: Welcome small bird's class

parts.note: ave is Latin for hail, a word of welcome

explanation.surface: Greeting a little bird of some social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological taxonomy, the class containing all birds has this Latin name.

clue.text: Declare a vicar has turned up

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: Announcing that a clergyman has appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert, so it means to declare.

clue.text: Hard to translate verse? Easy at first

indicators.note: to translate is to change into another form, so the letters of verse are rearranged
at first means only the opening letter of the word Easy is taken

explanation.surface: Poetry is hard to translate, though easy to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to translate' turns VERSE into SEVER; 'at first' takes E from 'Easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh, strict or demanding, so it means hard.

clue.text: Flatter male TV personage in the bar, last of all

indicators.note: last of all means the final letter of every one of the words that precede it is taken

explanation.surface: A man from television, in the pub, sweet-talks others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' wants to be the verb 'praise insincerely'; it is the comparative adjective 'more level'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more level or smooth is flatter, and something more even than another is the comparative here.
